context_label: Ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer
title: Bevacizumab every three weeks for ovarian cancer
schedule_label: First-line treatment starts with chemotherapy. Bevacizumab starts in cycle 2 and is given every 21 days. After up to six chemotherapy cycles it can continue alone, up to 15 months (22 cycles) in total. In platinum-resistant recurrence it is given every 21 days with five-day topotecan until progression or unacceptable side effects.
schedule_summary: First-line treatment starts with chemotherapy. Bevacizumab starts in cycle 2 and is given every 21 days. After up to six chemotherapy cycles it can continue alone, up to 15 months (22 cycles) in total. In platinum-resistant recurrence it is given every 21 days with five-day topotecan until progression or unacceptable side effects.
purpose: Your team may add bevacizumab to initial chemotherapy for advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer and then continue it alone. A different use is with five-day topotecan if the cancer has returned and is resistant to platinum.
indication_text: 00215a covers first-line FIGO IIIB, IIIC or IV epithelial ovarian, tubal or primary peritoneal cancer with carboplatin and paclitaxel. 00215c covers platinum-resistant recurrence with five-day topotecan after no more than two prior chemotherapy regimens and no prior VEGF-directed treatment.
administration_text: First-line treatment starts with chemotherapy. Bevacizumab starts in cycle 2 and is given every 21 days. After up to six chemotherapy cycles it can continue alone, up to 15 months (22 cycles) in total. In platinum-resistant recurrence it is given every 21 days with five-day topotecan until progression or unacceptable side effects.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver function. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, and blood pressure before and after treatment. The team checks your INR weekly until stable, then before each cycle. Symptoms, examination and scans according to your treatment plan.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Binds VEGF, a signal that promotes blood-vessel growth. Blocking VEGF can reduce the blood supply that supports tumour growth; it also affects normal blood vessels and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: Blocks the VEGF blood-vessel growth signal
visual: Less VEGF signalling supports tumour blood vessels
risks: Raised blood pressure and protein in the urine
Bleeding, blood clots and problems with wound healing
Rare bowel perforation, abnormal internal connections called fistulae, or serious wound infection
Rare severe headache, confusion, seizures or vision changes associated with a brain syndrome
Infusion reactions; fatigue and other effects may be increased by the chemotherapy partner
agents.watch: Report bleeding, severe pain, neurological symptoms or wound problems promptly, and attend blood-pressure and urine checks.
consent_risks: Head / vision
Severe headache, confusion, seizures or a change in vision need urgent help.
Heart / blood vessels
Attend blood-pressure checks; chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful leg need urgent help.
Kidneys / urine
Urine checks look for protein. Report new swelling, foamy urine or reduced urine.
Abdomen / bowel
Sudden severe abdominal pain needs urgent assessment.
Skin / wounds
Report bleeding or wounds that are painful, red, spreading or slow to heal.
Leg / clots
A new swollen painful leg or sudden breathlessness needs urgent help.

questions.q: What do I need to check before my next visit?
questions.a: Tell the team before dental surgery or an operation. Starting or restarting bevacizumab after major surgery requires adequate healing and at least 28 days.

support.title: Between visits
support.text: Call now for new severe abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, severe headache or a change in vision. Call 112 or 999 for sudden chest pain, severe breathlessness, seizure or stroke symptoms. With chemotherapy, fever, chills or suddenly feeling unwell also need urgent assessment.

teachback: Show which days you attend, which medicines you take beforehand and how to contact the 24-hour team.
consent_support: The prescriber will discuss the medicines on your individual plan. This sheet covers bevacizumab. Complete the separate consent for the selected chemotherapy partner before treatment.

evidence.title: GOG-0218
evidence.interpretation: Continuing bevacizumab after chemotherapy delayed progression in the first-line study.
evidence.limitations: The final analysis did not show an overall survival improvement across the whole study population. The first-line results do not estimate outcomes with five-day topotecan in recurrent disease.

local_adjuncts.directions: Take one capsule daily for four days starting on the day of chemotherapy.
Rinse 1 mL around the mouth four times daily after meals during the chemotherapy regimen.
Rinse 10 mL around the mouth for at least 1 minute four times daily; expel after rinsing.
Take one tablet three times daily as required.
Take 4 mg after the first episode of diarrhoea, then 2 mg after each further episode, to a maximum of 16 mg/day.

consent_choices.title: Bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report numbness and tell the nurse immediately if you flush or wheeze during treatment.
visual: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, hearing changes or an infusion reaction.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
agents.mechanism: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
visual: It reduces signals that help tumours form blood vessels. This can also affect blood pressure, kidneys and wound healing.
agents.watch: Call urgently for severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding, a new severe headache or sudden weakness.

agents.name: Topotecan infusion
agents.explanation: Topotecan blocks topoisomerase I, an enzyme that relieves strain while DNA is copied. Unrepaired DNA breaks can stop dividing cancer cells; healthy blood-forming and gut cells can also be affected.
agents.watch: Call oncology immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, severe tummy pain, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or new cough or breathlessness. Do not wait for the next cycle.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
Rare severe bowel inflammation or perforation
